A Codex switch no longer waits for Hermes to finish what it is doing. Installed on the owner's PC and used for a switch during a working agent session before release.

**What changed**

- **Codex switches go through even mid-session.** A switch no longer pauses Hermes or waits for running work, so it no longer gives up after a minute during a long agent session, and no message is turned away. A reply already running finishes on the account it started with; every chat uses the new account from its next message.
- **Your choice stays put.** A session that was running when you switched can save the old Codex order back when it renews a login or hits a rate limit. The switch keeps watching after it reports done and puts the account you chose back first within seconds, noting each fix in the receipt. It stops once the work that was running has finished.
- **The window warns if Codex is on the old account again.** If the account the last switch moved away from is first again, the Codex warning says so and asks you to switch again.
- A switch that still restarts the gateway (Claude provider older than 0.3.1) refuses while anything runs, as before.

**Known limit:** on a PC with many Hermes profiles the switch itself takes about a minute, because Hermes's own commands run once per profile. Chats keep working meanwhile. A faster switch is planned.

**After installing:** restart the gateway once, then fully close Hermes Desktop and open it again so it loads the new switch window.

The archive, its SHA-256 and the release gates are attached. Technical details are in `docs/release-notes.md`.
